text:
elaine: Quick thread — I pushed the per-client adaptive microbatch prototype to the staging pool and ran a mixed workload (70% streaming chat, 30% non-streaming completions). Perf summary attached.
mike: Nice. What was the target SLO and how did we configure adaptive_mb?
elaine: Target p95 = 150ms for streaming; p95 = 400ms OK for bulk. Config used: 
```
adaptive_mb: true
per_client_min: 1
per_client_max: 12
target_latency_ms: {streaming:150, completions:400}
kernel_reselect: auto
```
ashley: Raw numbers from the run (staging-gpu-a, 8xA100):
```
streaming, mb=1-3 dynamic: p50=40ms p95=145ms p99=320ms
completions, mb=8-12: p50=120ms p95=410ms p99=900ms
overall throughput ~ 6.2k tok/s per GPU
kv-cache miss spike correlated with p99 tail on streaming (see later)
```
sanjay: Was kernel reselecting frequently? recompile latency noise?
ashley: We saw ~2.2% of requests trigger kernel fallback on long sequences; reselect cost ~8-12ms one-off but sometimes cascades into tail when combined with kv miss.
tara: Do we have a trace showing correlation between kv miss, kernel reselect, and p99?
perf-bot: Profiling artifacts uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/perf/2246809456/ (cpu/kernels/kvcache/traces) :file_folder:
elaine: Short findings: most p99 events are 2-step: (1) request hits cold KV (spike in KV fetch ~60-200ms), (2) runtime attempts a different kernel due to sequence len/quantization path and stalls another ~10ms. Combined -> big tail.
mike: Hmm — sounds like two orthogonal mitigations: reduce KV cold miss probability (prefetch/pinned prefixes) and reduce kernel switches (stable kernel selection for streaming).
ashley: Agreed. Quick experiment results: forcing streaming to use kernel-v1 (stable, quant-friendly) and pin min_mb=2 gave: streaming p99 down from 320ms -> 210ms, p95 ~140ms unchanged. Bulk throughput dropped 4%.
sanjay: Is kernel-v1 slightly worse single-token throughput but more predictable?
ashley: Exactly. v2 gives ~6% faster median but has more path divergence with quant paths -> more reselects.
tara: For rollout plan: do we 1) pin kernel per-client-type 2) use per-client kv prewarm for active chats 3) enable adaptive_mb but bias streaming low? thoughts?
elaine: Proposed config snippet to test on prod-canary: 
```
route_policy: {
  streaming: { kernel: kernel-v1, min_mb: 2, max_mb: 6, kv_preheat: true },
  completions: { kernel: kernel-v2, min_mb: 6, max_mb: 12, kv_preheat: false }
}
```
mike: Sounds good. Add a guard: if model_seq_len > 2048, allow kernel-v2 for completions only.
perf-bot: Canary run scheduled for 2024-11-02T18:00Z, config: routes/streaming-kernel-v1-canary.json
ashley: Also adding a metric: counter for "compound_tail" events where kv_miss + kernel_reselect occur in same request.
sanjay: Nice. That will help quantify impact. Any concerns about cost? pinned prewarm increases token throughput and memory; estimate +6% GPU mem pressure.
elaine: OK tradeoff for SLA-critical streaming. For bulk customers we'll keep aggressive batching.
tara: Action items: (1) runtime team to push canary config (elaine) (2) perf to monitor compound_tail and p95/p99 dashboards (ashley) (3) infra to reserve a small RX pool for preheated KVs (sanjay)
elaine: I'll push the RFC and the canary PR this afternoon.
mike: If canary looks good we'll enable for 10% of streaming traffic then 50% over 48h.
ashley: One more note — need to adjust our autotuner to prefer stable kernels for short-latency routes; current objective strictly maximizes throughput which nudges it toward v2.
elaine: Good call. Add "latency_bias" flag to tuner.
ara: :thumbsup: (sorry, out of context ping — ignore)
runtime-bot: deploy triggered by elaine:pr/462 (canary config) :rocket:
elaine: Thanks everyone — will report canary metrics in this thread.
